title: How a candle burns, melting wax safely, and testing your wick
course_title: Candle Making: Safe Production of Container, Pillar and Event Candles

say: How a candle burns, melting wax safely, and testing your wick.
This is the video for module 1 of Candle Making: Candle Science and Safety.
Think of a candle as a small fuel system. The wax is the fuel.

say: The wick is the pump. Heat melts wax into a shallow melt pool, and the wick soaks it up like a cloth soaks up water.

say: The flame is the engine. The wax turns to hot gas at the top of the wick and burns, and that heat melts more wax.

For any wax, ask your supplier for the product data sheet with its temperatures, and use a thermometer every time. Guessing by eye is the main reason beginners get bad results.

say: Step 1. Work at a stable table away from curtains, gas cylinders and anything that can burn.

panel.heading: Set up a safe melting station
items: Stable table, away from curtains and gas cylinders
Use a double boiler: wax jug inside a pot of water
Top up the water; keep water out of the wax
Lid, fire blanket and oven gloves within reach
Children and pets out of the room

say: Step 2. Use a double boiler: a large pot of water with your metal jug of wax standing inside. The water stops the wax getting hotter than boiling water.

say: Step 3. Keep the water topped up, and keep water out of the wax, because it spits and burns.

say: If wax catches fire, turn off the heat if it is safe, and slide a metal lid or fire blanket over the pot. Leave it covered until cold.

panel.heading: If wax catches fire

cards.d: Turn off the heat if safe. Slide a metal lid or fire blanket over the pot. Leave it until cold.
Water turns to steam at once and throws burning wax out of the pot. Do not carry the pot outside.
If the fire is not out at once, get everyone out of the house and call for help.

say: Never pour water on a wax fire. It turns to steam and throws burning wax out of the pot.

say: The wick decides how a candle behaves. Too small, and it burns a tunnel. Too big, and you get soot and a hot jar. So you test.
For example, Folake in Ibadan has a jar 7.5 cm wide. She tries 2 wick sizes next to each other on her supplier's chart.

panel.heading: Folake's burn test: wick A or B?

say: Wick A makes a melt pool of 4.0 cm after 1 hour and 5.5 cm after 2 hours. At 3 hours it is still short of the edge, and starting to tunnel.

panel.heading: Folake's burn test: wick A or B?

say: Wick B reaches 7.0 cm at 2 hours with a calm flame, and the full edge by hour 3 with no smoke. Wick B wins, and she writes it on a recipe card.

panel.heading: Folake's burn test: wick A or B?

say: Test safely. Stay in the room, and burn on a metal tray or ceramic plate away from draughts. Trim the wick to about 6 mm. Use a snuffer, never water. Stop when about 1.3 cm of wax is left.

panel.heading: Every test candle
items: Stay in the room the whole time
Metal tray or ceramic plate, no draughts
Trim the wick to about 6 mm
Put it out with a snuffer, never water
Stop when about 1.3 cm of wax is left

say: To remember. The wick feeds the flame. Follow the data sheet and use a thermometer. Use a double boiler and never leave it. Smother a wax fire, never water. And burn test every new wick.

panel.heading: Remember
items: The wick carries melted wax up to the flame
Follow each wax's data sheet and use a thermometer
Double boiler, and never leave wax alone
Wax fire: lid or fire blanket, never water
Wick size causes most burning problems; test it

say: Now build your melting station and stick up your fire plan card: heat off, cover with lid, never water. Then run your first burn test and save the winner. Continue with the lessons below.

panel.heading: Your practice tasks
items: Build your safe melting station
Write your 3-line fire plan card
Run a 3-hour burn test with 2 wicks
Save the winning wick on a recipe card
